Spot Bitcoin ETFs bled $3.3 billion over 30 days, undercutting the long-term investors Standard Chartered counts on for its outlook.

Standard Chartered's Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) target of $500,000 by 2030 is one of Wall Street's boldest forecasts. However, a significant drop in November has put that target further out of reach. The bank's analyst Geoffrey Kendrick confirmed this ambitious goal in April, but Bitcoin fell 11.8% in just a week, closing at a 90-day low of $62,997 on November 18.

Currently, Bitcoin trades around $62,685, down 50.3% from its all-time high of $126,080 set on October 6, 2025. Given ETF outflows and tightening Federal Reserve policies, how realistic is Standard Chartered's Bitcoin target?

Mindscape studio / Shutterstock.com
Bitcoin Needs a 698% Increase to Hit $500,000
William Potter / Shutterstock.com

To reach $500,000 from its current price, Bitcoin needs to appreciate about 698%, nearly an eightfold increase. Bitcoin's market value, or market cap, is calculated by multiplying the price of a single coin by the total number of coins in circulation, and it stands at about $1.26 trillion. If Bitcoin reached $500,000 with 20,113,584 coins in circulation, its market value would be around $10.06 trillion.

The potential supply could push that figure even higher. Bitcoin's design limits the total supply to 21 million coins. Miners continue to add new coins until this cap is reached, so more coins may be circulating by 2030. At the same $500,000 price, that could imply a market value exceeding $10.06 trillion. This also applies to its previous high, as $126,080 now represents a larger market value than in October 2025.

Blue-chip stocks are often associated with established businesses, strong financial positions, and the ability to generate returns over extended periods. title: Is A Fed Hike Still Good News For JPMorgan?
detail:
Is A Fed Hike Still Good News For JPMorgan?
Trefis Team
Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:04 AM PST 6 min read
JPM
^GSPC
KRE
XLF
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Most investors expect a Fed rate hike to be good news for big banks like JPMorgan Chase. Higher rates let a bank charge more on its loans. On our data, that still holds for the business. It does not hold for the stock.

The short answer is no. Over 21 Fed hikes since June 2006, a fund of big financial stocks beat the S&P 500 in the next three months only 6 times. JPMorgan beat it after 8 of them. Since the latest hike, JPMorgan has lagged the S&P 500 so far, while that fund has beaten it.

How have bank stocks done since the September hike?

The Fed's rise in the top of its target range to 4.0% took effect on Sept 17, 2026. It was its first increase since the one that took effect on July 27, 2023. From the close the day before through Wednesday's close, JPMorgan returned -6.6%, counting dividends. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF, called SPY, returned -2.9%.

Two other big banks did worse. Bank of America returned -15.5% and Citigroup -11.3%. Wells Fargo returned -6.5%, about the same as JPMorgan. Our data shows no single confirmed cause for these drops.

JPMorgan has lost 6.6%, counting dividends, since the Fed hike that many owners expected to help it. If JPMorgan is a big part of your savings, that is a fall you have had to sit through. When the market has fallen, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has lost about 81 cents for every $1 its benchmark lost, on average. See the HQ record.

Did bank stocks ever rise and fall with rates?

They did, day to day. We measured how closely each stock's daily move tracked the daily change in the 2-year Treasury yield. That yield follows where traders expect Fed rates to go. The measure is called correlation. A high positive score means the two moved together, and a score near zero means no link.

From 2016 to 2019, the yearly score of the Financial Select Sector SPDR fund (XLF) averaged 0.52. JPMorgan's averaged 0.51. In 2026 so far, XLF's score is -0.09 and JPMorgan's is -0.04. The SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF (KRE), a fund of smaller banks, is at -0.19.

Put simply, bank stocks no longer rise on days when rate expectations rise. SPY now has a negative score too, at -0.13. We think higher yields are trading as bad news for stocks in general.

title: Citigroup Targets $5T in Client Wealth: Can Organic Growth Pay Off?
detail:
Citigroup Targets $5T in Client Wealth: Can Organic Growth Pay Off?
Nikita Kataruka
Thu, November 19, 2026 at 7:08 AM PST 3 min read
C
JPM
MS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup C is sharpening its wealth management strategy by targeting approximately $5 trillion in assets that existing clients hold with competing financial institutions. Rather than pursuing large acquisitions, the banking giant intends to capture a greater share of these assets through organic expansion. The strategy could strengthen Citigroup's wealth franchise while limiting acquisition-related costs and integration risks.

The opportunity is significant, considering Citigroup currently manages approximately $1.4 trillion in client balances. By deepening relationships with existing customers, the bank could increase investment assets, generate recurring fee income and improve cross-selling opportunities. Its integrated banking and wealth management capabilities provide a foundation for attracting additional client assets.

Recent performance underscores the strategy's potential. In the third quarter of 2026, Citigroup's wealth revenues increased 15% year over year to $3.27 billion, while net new investment assets reached a record $38 billion. Wealth net income surged 93% to $585 million. These improvements indicate stronger business momentum and suggest that expanding client relationships could support profitability and operating leverage.

Citigroup is also leveraging its investment banking ("IB") relationships and retail presence to accelerate wealth expansion, particularly across Asia. The region's growing affluent population offers opportunities to expand advisory services and investment products. Meanwhile, continued adviser hiring and AI-powered tools could improve client engagement, productivity and service delivery, supporting scalable growth.

Overall, Citigroup's organic wealth expansion strategy could diversify revenues, strengthen client retention and support management's broader profitability objectives without significant acquisition-related capital commitments. However, intense competition from established wealth managers, elevated technology and hiring expenses, and market volatility could constrain asset inflows and near-term margins.

How Citigroup Stacks Up Against Peers

Other major wealth management players, including Morgan Stanley MS and JPMorgan Chase JPM, are also capitalizing on rising demand for investment advisory services, expanding client relationships and increasing assets under management ("AUM").

Morgan Stanley continues to strengthen its wealth management franchise through adviser-led relationships, workplace solutions and investment products. In the third quarter of 2026, its Wealth Management division generated record revenues of $9.1 billion, up 10% year over year, while attracting $232.4 billion in net new assets. Total wealth management client assets reached $8.4 trillion.

Morgan Stanley's established distribution network, extensive adviser base and integrated IB capabilities position it to capture additional client assets and expand recurring fee revenues.

Similarly, JPMorgan is leveraging its extensive banking network, private banking capabilities and investment management offerings to deepen relationships with affluent clients. In the third quarter of 2026, JPMorgan's Asset & Wealth Management revenues increased 14% year over year to $6.9 billion. AUM rose 13% to $5.2 trillion, supported by continued inflows and higher market levels.

Both Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan possess considerably larger wealth management franchises than Citigroup, creating competitive challenges for its organic expansion strategy. However, Citigroup's focus on capturing assets already held by existing customers could provide a differentiated growth opportunity without requiring major acquisitions.

Chicago, IL – November 19, 2026 – Zacks Equity Research shares Dell Technologies DELL as the Bull of the Day and DraftKings DKNG as the Bear of the Day. In addition, Zacks Equity Research provides analysis on JPMorgan JPM, Bank of America BAC and Citigroup C.

Here is a synopsis of all five stocks:

Bull of the Day:

Dell Technologies is aZacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) that builds the servers, storage, networking gear and PCs behind enterprise computing. The company has become one of the largest suppliers of AI server infrastructure in the world.

The AI trade has lost a lot of air this fall, and with that, DELL has been pulled down to levels not seen since June. Even so, the earnings, the guidance and the estimates all still point higher.

All the negative sentiment over the last month has given long-term investors a chance to buy the AI build-out at a discount.

About the Company

Dell is headquartered in Round Rock, Texas, and was founded in 1984.

The company runs two main segments:

- Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) covers servers, storage and networking.

-Client Solutions Group (CSG) covers commercial and consumer PCs.

Dell now gets most of its revenue from ISG, and that segment is growing fastest. AI servers built on the latest GPU platforms are driving that shift, along with a long refresh cycle for traditional servers.

The company is currently valued at $205 billion and has a forward PE of 12. The stock has Zacks Style Scores of "C" in Value, "B" in Growth, and "D" in Momentum.

The AI Bubble Lets Out Some Air

There's no sugarcoating it: AI stocks have had a rough stretch.

NVIDIA has led the space lower, and investors have been selling anything tied to AI hardware first and asking questions later. Dell is down almost 50% from its September high.

The selling assumes the AI spending cycle is peaking. The demand data from Dell's most recent quarter questions that bearish narrative.

Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance

On September 1, Dell reported EPS of $7.04, crushing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.95 by 42%. Revenues reached a record $47.0 billion, topping the $45.3 billion consensus.

Growth was broad-based with ISG revenue surging 89% y/y to $31.8 billion, led by a 122% jump in traditional servers and networking.  CSG revenue climbed 20% to $15.0 billion. Non-GAAP operating income more than doubled to $5.93 billion.

AI demand was the biggest driver as Dell booked a record $60.9 billion in AI orders and ended the quarter with a record $95 billion backlog. Management noted that its pipeline remains a multiple of that backlog, following $131.7 billion in orders over the past 12 months. Dell's AI customer base has also surpassed 6,500.

Rising rates widen bank profit spreads: U.S. Bancorp's net interest margin climbed to 2.84% from 2.75%, as assets reprice faster than funding costs.

Interest rates are rising again, putting bank dividend payers back in focus for income investors. The Federal Reserve raised the upper bound of its target range to 4.00% on September 17, 2026, up from 3.75%. The 10-year Treasury yield stood at 5.06% on November 18, compared with 4.12% a year earlier, after topping out at 5.31% on October 5. This matters to bank shareholders because of net interest income (NII), the gap between what a bank earns on loans and securities and what it pays depositors.

YinYang / Getty Images

When asset yields rise faster than deposit costs, that spread widens, and the extra profit funds dividend increases. Four of the five banks below raised their quarterly payouts in 2026. The fifth has held its payout steady.

All five banks slashed their dividends during the 2008 to 2009 financial crisis, and one of them cut again in 2020. Each bank's case rests on its record since the recovery, its current earnings coverage, and its capital levels.

Citigroup: A 12% Raise Backed by a Low Payout

Citigroup (NYSE: C) yields 2.27% at a recent price of $118.20. In 2026, it raised its quarterly dividend from $0.60 to $0.67, which management called a 12% increase.
